data.claim: With only HOME and PATH, _prepare leaves git without an identity and commit exits 128; adding the four GIT_ variables to the lane env makes commit exit 0 while `git config --global --list` stays empty in the lane.
data.falsifier: Commit still fails with the four variables set, or `git config --global --list` shows content in the lane.
data.mechanism: git reads user.* from config under HOME; _prepare replaces HOME and passes only named variables, so the global file is out of reach. GIT_AUTHOR_* and GIT_COMMITTER_* outrank config and need no file.

Also measured: this repo has no local user.name, git reports scope global, so a strict --local read would refuse every lane here; the fix reads git's resolved value from the worktree.

data.alternatives: ddflow@localhost placeholder: refused by the coordinator, it would misattribute lane work. Exposing [REDACTED:path] to the lane: refused by the operator's brief. Fixing only opencode.prepare: leaves other lanes uncovered.
data.consequences: A lane in a repo with no identity no longer starts; before, it started and failed at its first commit. The refusal has no off switch.
data.context: B6a483bb0f5: the private HOME hides the launcher's git config, so a lane commit exits 128. The operator asked that the lane's HOME stay private and identity be passed explicitly. Identity on this host is in global scope, none in the repo, so the read must be the resolved value: a --local read would refuse every lane.
data.decision: _prepare reads user.name and user.email as git resolves them in the lane's cwd and passes them as GIT_AUTHOR_* and GIT_COMMITTER_* values. A variable the spec sets stays. A work tree with no identity refuses the launch, with no placeholder and no knob. A lane with no cwd or outside any work tree gets none. Coordinator call relayed to lane sw-gitident on 2026-11-05, not an operator choice: r-safe-by-default wants the operator to choose enforcement, so the refusal default awaits the operator's confirmation.
data.title: A lane gets the git identity as values, and a work tree with none refuses the launch

chunk_findings.detail: `_identity` runs `git config --get user.name` and `--get user.email` without `--local`, so Git falls back to the launcher's global/system config. Given a repository whose `.git/config` has no `user.name` or `user.email` but the launcher's `[REDACTED:path]` has both, `_identity` returns those global values instead of the required `failed(...has no git user.name or user.email...)`. This violates the intent that identity is read from the repo and that a repo with no identity refuses the launch, and it exposes the operator's global identity values from `[REDACTED:path]` to the lane.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/lane_headless.py:_identity

chunk_findings.detail: The test helper function `run_lane` calls `time.sleep(0.02)` in a tight polling loop to wait for a headless lane process to terminate, with a 30-second deadline. This introduces inefficient busy-waiting that can slow down test suites and cause flakiness under high system load where thread scheduling or process start times exceed the 20ms poll interval.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_lane_git_identity.py:59

chunk_findings.detail: If a repo defines only `user.name` and the lane environment carries `EMAIL` (for example `[lanes].pass_env` includes `EMAIL=[REDACTED:email]`), Git itself uses that `EMAIL` as the committer/author email fallback when `user.email` is unset, so `git commit` would succeed. But `_identity` never consults `env["EMAIL"]`; it runs `git config --get user.email`, sees no value, appends `user.email` to `absent`, and returns a failed `Result`, causing `_prepare` to refuse the launch even though the lane could commit. This contradicts the added doc statement that the values are captured “as git resolves them there”.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/lane_headless.py:_identity

chunk_findings.detail: The bug fix B6a483bb0f5 is a task, but the change contains no task file naming its phase, dependencies, and wave tag. This violates [r-task-phase-needs-wave], which requires every bug-fix task to carry a phase, stated needs, and a wave:N tag; without the task file, `ddflow waves --stamp` cannot stamp this work.

chunk_findings.detail: The test helper `run_lane` calls `lh.ProcessHeadless()` and constructs a `ld.LaunchSpec`, but passes `**kw` directly to `ld.LaunchSpec`. However, `ld.LaunchSpec` does not accept arbitrary keyword arguments such as `home` (used on line 105: `run_lane(COMMIT, str(repo), home=home)`), which will raise a `TypeError: LaunchSpec.__init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'home'`.

It used one review round and set critic failed with 11 findings at head 6b1dcdcc1. Owner told by message; no record was altered.

data.rule: Lanes of one session share one scratchpad directory. Do not keep an executable there under a generic name and re-run it later: another lane can overwrite it, and you then act on that lane's item as that agent. Run commands inline, or name the file after the lane and read it back before each run. A refusal naming a pid, item or agent you do not recognise means stop and look at what you actually ran before suspecting the tool.
data.summary: The scratchpad is shared by every lane of the session, so a generic script name there can be replaced by another lane. Run commands inline or use lane-named files read back before each run.
data.title: Never run a generically named script from a scratchpad lanes share: another lane's script runs under its identity
data.why: sw-gitident's review.sh was overwritten by sw-pilottoy's at the same path. A re-run reviewed SW-pilot-toy under sw-pilottoy's name and used one of its review rounds. An earlier refusal naming the other lane's pid had been read as a possible ddflow defect, when it was correct.
